acceptance: The PR names the package and the test that left the tmux server alive, with the log or artifact line as evidence
A regression test fails when a test leaves a tmux server alive after it ends, or the PR records that #1141 covers it with the test that proves it
Three consecutive main runs of the Go 1.27 job finish within the 60 min job limit
fix: Find the test that starts tmux server 18408's socket without a cleanup on ubuntu Go 1.27 (the uploaded test-integration.json and test-rusage.ndjson name the packages that ran real tmux). Confirm #1141's orphan-server cleanup covers that package on ubuntu; else give that test a per-test socket with a t.Cleanup kill-server, and add a regression test that fails when a test leaves a tmux server alive.
summary: Main run 40265789886 (6cbf1a765, started 2026-10-26 03:47 UTC): the job `go / build + test (Go 1.27, ubuntu, every package, no gates)` (job 121387919906) stayed in the step `test (race + cover, incl. integration tier)` until a cancel at 08:54:56 UTC; every other job ended by 04:05. Job log evidence: the last package line is `ok go/test/structure 6.513s` at 03:54:43, then no output for 5 h. At cleanup the runner terminated orphan processes hostsampler (3891), make (3900), sh (3904) and `tmux: server` (18408). So go test finished its packages, and a tmux server that a test started (and left alive) kept the step pipe open, so make and sh never exited. make test-integration bounds each package with -timeout 20m (go/Makefile:117,124), which cannot catch a survivor after the test binary ends. PR #1141 (no orphan tmux server, bounded integration waits) fixes a hang of the same shape on macOS. PR #1152 bounds each go.yml job to 60 min, so a repeat now fails the job instead of holding main's concurrency group.
title: Find why the Go 1.27 ubuntu test step of main run 40265789886 hung for more than 4 h
